speaker: Other
text: year 2016 we began face funding the replacement of our salt dome. The original salt dome was constructed in the late 70s and in 2016 it started showing signs of fatigue. This resulted in the issuance of an RFP for the replacement of the salt dome in April of 2019. At that time we received bids that were far higher than we originally budgeted. Staff proposed an additional phase of funding which was realized in the current fiscal year or 2021. As part of the original RFP a structural analysis was performed to determine if the existing dome was suitable for any rehabilitation instead of replacement. The analysis determined that the dome was in poor condition had exceeded its lifespan and warranted replacement in the next one to two years. In the five years since the replacement of the dome was originally placed in the CIP it has continued to deteriorate and many of you may remember during the one of the strategic planning meetings had a visual I wish I had today with salt pouring up the side from a hole in their current salt dome. On Thursday March the 25th we received three sealed proposals for the reissued salt dome replacement RFP. This was requested a like-for-like concrete structure in the same location. In an effort to determine the most cost effective solution we also got proposals for wooden structures. Upon reviewing the proposals the wooden domes proposed by bulk storage were the lowest bids and South Industries were the lowest bids for the concrete dome came in second. The difference in the cost between these two was much less than we initially anticipated. So to get a good understanding of what this would entail staff actually visited five different sites with a mix of concrete domes and wooden domes. The respective wooden domes showed significant distress, multiple extensive repairs, and a failing shingle system in all cases. They also have a shorter lifespan. The indications from our counterparts were that the wooden structures were required ongoing relatively expensive maintenance and both on a routine basis and to mitigate expected failures. While the concrete domes also require maintenance it is much less frequent than the wooden domes. The effects of maintenance are much longer lasting toward protecting the integrity of the structure. The new dome will also be fully insulated unlike our existing dome which is bare concrete. Although the concrete dome proposed by South Industries is not the lowest bid and is $29,070 over the current budget amount it is our opinion that this will be the longest lasting solution requiring the least amount of maintenance and reflecting the best value of money for the long term of the city. Funding to cover this overage is available through savings from our front-end loader which Council just approved and has come in under budget. Based on these facts and the additional due diligence performed by staff and the increased useful life of a concrete structure versus a wooden structure, staff and I recommend that Council award the bid for the DPS salt dome replacement to South Industries for a project cost of $654,108.

So anybody is welcome to join us. If you do join us, please, you know, stay socially distant and wear a mask. Also, I'm going to encourage everyone, if you haven't done it yet to get vaccinated. There have been opportunities for walk-in clinics recently right here in our city. Thank you, Mayor Grafstein for making sure those are happening. I appreciate that. And I would just really encourage everybody to do it. I recently had my mother recently encountered someone who was COVID positive and she didn't know it. And, but I am feeling good because my mother is fully vaccinated. And so I'm not as worried about her getting sick anymore. I also want to say thank you to all those that participated in the 5K last weekend, a great event. I am not a runner, so I was not there running, but good job to all of you that did. And I am a walker though. So on Tuesday, May 11th is the first treads on Tuesday walking club. We're meeting at the civic center at the gazebo in front of civic center. And we'll walk at civic center park together. It is open to everybody. Please join us at 7 PM on the May 11th, young and old. We will enjoy, and I'm sure we'll get shirts at some point. I also want to note that there is a native plant sale that is being planned for the end of May. And there will be, keep an eye out for information about pre-orders for that native plant sale. So you can plan your gardens and figure out what you want to order before you get there. And they'll have them all boxed up and ready to go so that you can just come pick them up. And in the funds from that sale, we'll go towards the bloom project and the ECC to plant more native gardens here in our city. I also want to note that the friends of the library are an awesome group that are doing some really great things, but they have a kids book and paperback book pop-up sale that is coming in May, May 22nd as well, from like one to four so keep an eye out for that. And they have changed the way that they do their pop-up sales typically now. So it's a, give what you think it's worth. So anybody's welcome to come and find some great books for their family. And then my last thing was Muse. I wrote down Muse because I was thinking we approved the salt dome and the last dome lasted for about 40 years. And 40 years from now, it's going to be 2061. And maybe we won't even have cars. Maybe we'll have flying vehicles and we won't need ice domes anymore. Anyway, have a great night. Thank you.

speaker: davidsoltis
text: Yeah, so every year I talk on, when we give a proclamation for the National Police Officers Memorial Week, each year I go over, I think what are statistics that need to be talked about, especially deaths in the line of duty. So if we look at 2020, there were recorded 360 fallen officers that were fallen across or killed across this country. In 2021, in just a few months, there's been 103. And if you look at the breakdown, there's about 17 that were died in gunfire, and the rest were motorcycle crash, stabbing. And then actually there's been about 13 were killed by a vehicle of some sort. They were ran down. So I just think, you know, our police department, I agree with the rest of the council, our police department is top-notch. It's fantastic. That's what we wanted, and they are giving exactly what we asked for. We started SIU, which you see by the data. It's an incredible undertaking, the chief and the police department, our police department. And it's doing exactly what we want it to do. And so I can't be prouder of our men and women in blue and what they do, as well as the ones that take the 911 calls, operators. They do a fantastic job under such tremendous stress. Like I've said before, I work EMS, and it's incredible stress at times. Things become crazy and havoc, and so, you know, their expertise and their professionalism is beyond compare. And so I just wanted to make some of those comments about other officers. I did go to, well, since COVID, they haven't had it, at least I don't think they have had it every year. There's a church in Hazel Park that puts on the blue light memorial for all the fallen officers. And so the families would come to this get together. It's kind of a mass, and it's just incredible. The pain that some of these families are still going through with their loved ones being struck down in the line of duty. In fact, I sat next to a relative of a young guy. He was a Wayne State police officer, and he was senselessly struck down and killed. And it's just very heart aching to see that. But I think everyone should at least make an attempt to visit it at some point in time. But that's all I have. Thank you.

speaker: roslyngrafstein
text: Thank you. I've got a few things on the vaccine. So I think at this point, anyone who is able to get out to get a vaccine, anyone who is able and who is eligible is getting one. A couple of months ago, the big issue was finding a place to get the vaccine. And I had to leave the city. My family had to leave the city. Just there wasn't anything here. There weren't things necessarily close. I was hearing people who were going out of state, who were driving four hours away. And over the last month, that has significantly changed. The pharmacy shop now has walk-in for Pfizer, Moderna, and Johnson & Johnson, which they're no longer pausing that. That one is available again. So he sent me a message this afternoon that he's got all three of them available for walk-ins. So if you wanna just go, you can get there. There's a lot of places getting appointments. I held another clinic today at the Venetian Club. When we did this a few weeks ago, it was 300 doses of Pfizer. I specifically picked Pfizer because the 16 and 17-year-olds were able to do that. And within 24 hours, it was full. The pharmacist called me last week and said, I have another 400. And I said, that's great. It will fill up again. And it didn't. We had just over 100 people who came through today. And over time, we reduced that number from 400 down so that they weren't gonna have any that were wasted. And I think it's just that people are able to get it so many places. So if you're still on the fence, do your research. You need to do what works for you. But if you do wanna move ahead and get the vaccine, there are multiple places that you can get it now. There seems to be almost a surplus. So just thank you to everyone who is helping and who helped get out the word about these clinics. I also want to talk about the 5K. So I am not much of a runner, but I ran my first 5K in that I ran, walked, ran, walked back and forth, back and forth. Started with the run, ended with a run, did a walk. I think I probably ran about two miles in there, but it was everybody. There was, you know, someone was there with, he had his child in a stroller. There were people who were younger, older. There's a lot of different people there. I talked to someone who came in from Mount Kleinman's. He said this was the only one he could find in the area. So it was nice to get out and to do that. And the weather cooperated, which was great because so often we have rain for that. So that was really great. So thank you to Brooke Heisler and everyone who put that on. Also wanna talk about our police department. Chief Haynes, again, you guys are doing a great job. I'm getting, because I'm getting so many compliments. And I also want to talk a little bit about child abuse prevention. So I think Mr. Stoltz has mentioned it. Last time I'm wearing my pinwheel for Child Abuse Prevention Month, I was contacted, I'm gonna be very careful how I say this because I wanna keep an anonymity, but I was contacted by a mother who was the victim of abuse. Abuse. And she had nothing but good to say about our police department. The police came and she was grateful. I am grateful. And there's children. And so often we think about the adults and we think about a woman who's being abused. And you have to remember that a child who grows up with abuse is going to grow up thinking that this is normal. It's normal for them to become an abuser. It's normal for them to be abused. Doesn't always happen that way, but so often it does. So the police came in and I said to her, she contacted me after the fact. And I said to her, don't ever be scared to call the police. Their job is to protect you. They will protect you. They will protect your children. So I just, so I'm saying this to everybody. If you are concerned about calling the police, if you feel you are in danger, our police are there to protect you and to protect your children. What else? Okay. This is, you know, this is the police officers memorial week proclamation and we did the proclamation, but it got me thinking in September, it will be 20 years since 9-11. And I don't know what we can do, but I would like to somehow commemorate our first responders, you know? And so I'm open to suggestions. I don't know what the world is going to look like COVID wise. So I'm open to suggestions. So if anyone is interested, anyone in the public is interested in, then it's something that I would like to do. This Saturday, as Councilor Moorabach mentioned, we will be doing the Arbor Day tree planting. I don't think, well, last year in June, we did the trees on Mulan. We did that with the ECC and we had the men's club and some other volunteers who came out. So if you're interested in being a sponsor for that, please reach out, let me know. You can contact myself, you can contact Mrs. Marsh, but really excited about that coming to the city.
